Loading libraries
```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(flexdashboard)
library(p8105.datasets)
  data("instacart")
```

Loading data
```{r}
instacart_df = 
  instacart |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  group_by(
    product_id, product_name, department
  ) |> 
  summarize(
    n_purchases = n(),
    mean_cart_position = mean(add_to_cart_order),
    reorder_rate = mean(reordered)
  ) |> 
  ungroup()

instacart |> 
  count(department) |> 
  arrange(desc(n)) |> 
  print(n=21)
```

### Scatterplot: 
Relationship between average cart position and reorder rate across departments
* no missing variables through skimr on instacart
* used view(instacart_df) to evaluate that mean_cart position follows a right skewed histogram distribution
* skimr on instacart_df showed that p75 for n_purchases was 18 and p100 was 18726 so decided to use 20 as cutoff point
* After finding `r n_distinct(pull(instacart, department))` departments, I used print(n=21) to list the total number of categories; i removed "missing" category in my department filter
* scatter plot shows that if the product was placed earlier in the cart, it tended to be reordered more. Purplish categories seem to be scattered throughout the plot, most distinctly around earlier mean cart position and higher reorder rating. snacks are notably concentrated around the middle of the cart with an average reorder_rate
```{r}
instacart_df |> 
  filter(department %in% c("dairy eggs", "produce", "canned goods", "beverages", "deli", "snacks", "pantry", "frozen", "meat seafood", "household", "bakery", "personal care", "dry goods pasta", "babies", "other", "breakfast", "international", "alcohol", "bulk", "pets")) |> 
  filter(n_purchases >=19) |> 
  mutate(text_label = str_c("Product: ", product_name, "\nPurchases: ", n_purchases)) |> 
  plot_ly(
    x = ~mean_cart_position,
    y = ~reorder_rate,
    type = "scatter",
    mode = "markers",
    color = ~department,
    colors = "viridis",
    text = ~text_label,
    alpha = 0.5
  )
```

### Scatterplot: 
Number of products per order against day of the week
* days of the week are not given but if 0 represents monday then the monday seems to have the most number of products per order, and tuesday has the greatest variability and outliers in the number of products purchased per order
```{r}
instacart |> 
  group_by(order_id, order_dow) |> 
  summarize(n_products = n()) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  mutate(order_dow = as.factor(order_dow)) |> 
  plot_ly(
    x = ~order_dow,
    y = ~n_products,
    color = ~order_dow,
    type = "box",
    colors = "viridis"
  )
```
